note: Standing owner rules from reviews. Every agent reads these before writing or designing, and every design is run through shrih_agent/design_rules_agent.py (python run_agent.py design-check ...), which applies the rules that carry a "check" automatically and returns the fix. When the owner gives a new rule: add it with run_agent.py add-rule, and if it can be measured, add a check to design_rules_agent.py and name it here.

rules.rule: An approved design is a quality bar, never a template: every post is a completely new design, not the same layout with new text.
We make real-estate content that preserves the real building; the building's architecture must never change.
The building is the hero: headline and text go in the sky above it or in the foreground below it, never over the building, and no dark gradient may cover the facade.
Do not repeat the same elements between posts (same fact boxes, same split gold/navy call-to-action bar); give each post its own call-to-action treatment.
Use a different render each time (21 renders in assets/renders and assets/original) and do not stick to one colour scheme; vary palette and fonts per post.
For a brand announcement the brand comes first: its logo or name leads, then 'is coming to Shrih Plaza' (e.g. Domino's first, then 'is coming to', then Shrih Plaza).

Use the official Shrih Plaza logo, assets/original/logo-official.png (olive-gold gradient Shri + Plaza lockup with the two hanging lines, source D:/shrih plaza/Untitled design.png with its white background removed, final choice by the owner 2026-10-01), and only the 12 approved brands; never the older posts' extra brands or old phone numbers. Phone: +91 90564 53575.

Workflow: images are made in Adobe (Generative Expand plus sky/lighting grades on the real renders), laid out in Claude Design, and finished in Adobe Express Pro; posts can also be turned into animated reels.

The Shrih Plaza logo must be big and prominent, never a small corner mark: the official wide lockup at about 36-54% of the canvas width (roughly 390-580 px on a 1080 px post or reel, 150-230 px tall). Owner asked twice for a bigger logo (2026-10-01).

Place brand logos cut out, without their white background box; on dark or brand-coloured backgrounds use a reversed version (white wordmark, e.g. assets/original/brands/dominos-reversed.png) with a soft white edge so the logo reads clearly.

Quality bar (owner was impressed, 2026-10-01): the 'Dusk Issue' magazine-cover carousel, where Adobe cuts out the sky so a giant masthead sits behind the roofline and the building stands in front of the text. Aim for this level of idea and depth on every post, but never reuse it as a template.

Take each post's colour theme from its own image: sample the photo's sky, light and facade colours and build the palette from them (e.g. sapphire sky + sunset gold + sandstone for a golden-hour render). Never lay an unrelated colour (like plum over a golden image) on a photo; it looks odd.

If the logo fades on a post's background, use a shade of it for that post only (same logo, same gradient): logo-official-deep.png on light/cream backgrounds, logo-official-rich.png (vivid warm gold) on saturated blue or brand-coloured backgrounds like Domino's blue, logo-official-light.png on dark navy or green, logo-official-champagne.png on bright blue skies. Aim for at least 3:1 contrast and a crisp, not washed-out, look.
Do not write "Artist's impression" anywhere on content (posts, stories, reels, captions). Owner decision 2026-10-01.

The logo's text (the 'Plaza' letters and the Shri mark) must be clearly readable on its real background, pixel by pixel, not just on average: median contrast at least 3:1 and the weakest 10% of logo pixels at least 2.5:1. If it fails, switch to the shade of the logo that passes (design_rules_agent.best_logo_for_region).

Logos and brand marks must be sharp, never blurry: the file must have at least 1.5x the pixels it is displayed at. If only a small file exists, rebuild it cleanly in the brand's flat colours at high resolution (see assets/original/brands/dominos-reversed.png, 1418 px) or use a vector, never stretch a small image.

Concepts the owner rejected as not up to mark (2026-10-01): the vintage tilted postcard with stamp and postmark, and plain full-bleed photo + headline layouts. The strong ideas are the ones where the building itself carries the concept (masthead behind the roofline; the same building split day/night). Build every new concept around the building, never around decoration.

Choose the hero image carefully: prefer renders with strong perspective, a big building and a dramatic sky (e.g. the ai-04 sunset corner view). Do not use the flat frontal daytime elevation for a hero post (owner: 'wrong choice of image'). A day/night split only works when the two halves are clearly different.

Logo colour: gold and its shades are the first preference, and the gold must LOOK gold. Pale shades (champagne, light) read as cream/white and are not acceptable when a vivid gold (official, deep, rich) can work. If no vivid gold reads on the background, deepen the sky behind it edge to edge (a full-width gradient in the image's own darkened colour, strongest at the top and fading out below the logo; never an oval or box patch, which looks separate) until rich gold passes (weakest 10% >= 3:1). Only if that fails, use a pale gold, then white or palette colours. Owner, 2026-10-01.

Keep the sky behind text calm: if the top of an image is busy with clouds (often after Adobe Generative Expand), smooth the upper sky into a clean gradient in the image's own colours, fading back to the real sky well above the roofline. Never touch the building. (Owner, sunset feed, 2026-10-01)

Every post follows the owner's content strategy (brand-kit/content-strategy.md): BRAND -> LOCATION -> COMMERCIAL ACTIVITY -> SHOP OWNERSHIP -> ENQUIRY. The brand or visual is only the hook; the design and caption must end on owning a commercial space at Shrih Plaza and an enquiry, never on visiting or enjoying a brand.
